name: Brandywine Valley & Wilmington
summary: The du Pont dynasty's green corner of Delaware — grand estates, one of the world's great gardens, and Wyeth country along the Brandywine.

lodging.name: A Brandywine Valley inn
lodging.blurb: Country inns among the estates north of Wilmington.

foodMustTry.name: Tax-free everything
foodMustTry.blurb: Delaware has no sales tax — a running theme in the First State.

days.label: Day 118 — The du Pont estates
days.summary: Gunpowder fortunes turned into mansions and gardens.

item.title: Winterthur Museum & Gardens
item.blurb: Henry Francis du Pont's 175-room house, filled with the country's premier Americana collection, in 1,000 acres of gardens.

item.title: Hagley Museum
item.blurb: The original du Pont black-powder mills on the Brandywine — where the whole dynasty (and DuPont) began.

days.label: Day 119 — Longwood & the riverfront
days.summary: One of the world's great gardens and Wilmington's revived waterfront.

item.title: Longwood Gardens
item.blurb: Pierre du Pont's spectacular 1,100-acre gardens and conservatory, just over the Pennsylvania line — fountains, forests, and glasshouses.

item.title: Wilmington Riverfront & Delaware Art Museum
item.blurb: The riverwalk and a strong collection of Pre-Raphaelite and American illustration art (Howard Pyle).

days.label: Day 120 — South to Dover
days.summary: Down the state to the capital.

commute.scenicNote: South down Delaware into the flat farm country around the capital.
